key_insight: By combining phase-amplitude reduction with sparse-sensor machine learning, the method rapidly retunes airfoil wake shedding while directly constraining lift fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical control strategy for post-stall airfoils and other periodic flow systems where fast frequency shifting is needed without inducing harmful aerodynamic variability.
method: Reconstruct the wake state from only three sparse sensors using nonlinear machine-learning-based inference.
Compute time-varying phase and amplitude sensitivity fields to locate optimal actuation timing and spatial forcing.
Derive an optimal waveform that speeds synchronization while penalizing amplitude deviations in the lift response.
evidence_signal: Across several NACA airfoils at post-stall angles of attack, the optimized forcing changed wake frequency faster than standard sinusoidal actuation and reduced lift fluctuations by 20% with amplitude penalty.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate sparse-sensor reconstruction and flow-specific sensitivity fields, so robustness may drop under strong noise, model mismatch, or off-design conditions.
paper_title: Machine-learning-assisted phase-amplitude reduction for fast synchronization of airfoil wakes with constrained fluctuations
